answer: Every agent identity must first complete a unique proof of computational work bound to its public key before it can transact: like a plume grown feather by feather, one identity costs one sequential computation that cannot be parallelized or replayed for a clone. A sybil voyage of a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand proofs, while an honest agent pays once and keeps its earned standing — yarrow roots spread slowly the same way, so growth that cannot be faked in bulk makes bulk fakery unprofitable.
